newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker in moderate trade.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker on Monday, extending Friday's decline as nervous investors await further comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan this week.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 11.86 points to finish at 6145.98, but recouped some early losses after a late surge in New York.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed over 41 points on Monday.

"It's a typical Monday market. A little bit of indecision in deciding which way to go, but we'll get a better direction perhaps on Tuesday," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
Greenspan's comments on the "irrational exuberance" of stock markets pushed share prices lower last week. He is scheduled to deliver congressional testimony on Wednesday.
In today's action, gold and consumer products led eight of Toronto's 14 sub-groups lower.
The TSE's strength lay in media and communications, base metals, and transportation. Trading volume totalled 96.3 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.02 billion).
Declining stocks outpaced advances 553 to 408 with 294 issues unchanged.
* Queenstake Resources Ltd. topped the most-active list, up 0.34 to close at 3.90 on 4.4 million shares. The mining stock earlier hit a 52-week high of 4.50.

Queenstake rallied on Friday on news of promising assay results from Francisco Gold Corp.'s El Sauzal gold property in Mexico. A Queenstake property is completely surrounded by the El Sauzai property.
* Cube Energy Corp. jumped 1.50 to 13 in light volume after the junior oil firm agreed to a C$62.3 million ($45 million) takeover offer from Barrington Petroleum Ltd.
* Liquor and entertainment giant Seagram Co. Ltd. fell 1.15 to 52.20, depressing the consumer products group.
